text:
pranav: Heads-up — saw 3 OOMs on p2-prod during the continuous-batching rollout (window ~ 17:20–17:40). Stack traces point to allocator failures when batch size expands mid-request. Suspect interplay between workspace sizing and per-seq KV cache overhead.

lina: Ugh. Any profiler traces or nvprof snapshots?

pranav: Pasted the relevant snippets below. Short summary: when batch grows from 8->18 in-flight, we allocate extra workspace per-kernel which temporarily spikes GPU mem ~+3.2GB. Allocator then fails on the kernel that does fused-attn because we hit fragmentation, not total mem.

jess: Can you paste the memmap/profile? also which kernel variants were chosen (fused vs generic)?

pranav: Sure — grabbing the perf log:
```
[perf] timeline: t0 allocate 1.2G workspace (fwd), t1 batch growth -> allocate 2.9G extra, t2 fused_attn_kernel_v2 chosen, t3 cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 512MB)
[allocator] free blocks: 128MB, 64MB, 32MB, 16MB scattered (total usable < requested due to fragmentation)
[kv-cache] hits: 72% prefix reuse, kv-cache per-seq overhead ~ 24KB * seq_len padding
```

sam: That matches a known failure mode: our allocator uses best-fit with coalescing disabled for short-lived workspaces. When batch growth causes many different-sized workspaces to be allocated concurrently, fragmentation skyrockets. We intentionally disabled coalescing to keep lock contention low, but that trades fragmentation for throughput.

lina: Are the workspace sizes deterministic per kernel? Could we bound them or reuse a pooled buffer keyed by max workspace class rather than exact size?

pranav: Workspaces vary by kernel variant and sequence-length distribution. Two levers proposed: 1) bucketed pooled allocator (power-of-two classes) for transient kernel workspaces, 2) conservative workspace cap policy during rapid batch-growth (delay choosing large-kernel variant until pool stabilized).

jess: Any perf regression risk if we force kernel fallback? Last time we forced generic kernels for memory safety we saw 8–12% p50 increase for short sequences. We need a canary and perf budget.

pranav: Agreed. I ran a quick microbenchmark on dev machines: pooling + reuse keeps p50 within +1.5% and reduces peak mem by ~2.8GB for mixed batch growth traces. Fallback-to-generic gave +9% p50 on our chat workload but prevented OOMs.

sam: Another quick mitigation: trim padding at batch boundary. Continuous batching currently pads all sequences to longest in-batch; with growth we re-pad repeatedly. If we record per-request max_seq and only pad when kernel is about to execute (lazy-padding) we can avoid transient padding blowups. That might be low-risk perf-wise.

jess: Sounds good. Can we calculate per-seq overhead and padding waste for the failing window? We need numbers for the post-mortem.

pranav: From telemetry for the incident window:
- average pad waste per request: 1.2k tokens total across KV+input padding (~420KB/request)
- concurrent inflight requests: 72 -> pad waste ~30MB (but when batch grew, repeated re-padding multiplied this)
- allocator fragmentation estimated wasted but reserved: ~1.6GB
- observed peak alloc spike: +3.2GB at t1

lina: OK. Proposed immediate action items:
1) deploy pooled power-of-two transient allocator behind flag (dev-only canary)
2) enable lazy-padding for continuous batching path
3) conservative kernel selection policy: if free_pool < threshold prefer memory-slim variant
4) add a perf smoke that simulates mid-request batch growth and check p50/p95 

jess: +1 on that list. Add an experiment to measure tail latency changes vs cost. Also capture nvprof snapshots for the next 24h for any OOM.

pranav: I'll open an RFC + rollout plan. For patching fast: implement pooled allocator feature-flagged in runtime, and lazy-pad toggle in batching layer. Sam, can you prototype pooling this afternoon? I can wire the telemetry and add alerts for allocator-frag > 1GB.

sam: Will do. I'll also add a quick script to simulate batch growth:
```
# simulate growth: spawn requests with seq lengths [32..1024] at varying inter-arrival, force batch growth mid-flight
python tools/sim_batch_growth.py --qps 150 --burst 30 --duration 600
```

infra-bot: Canary deployed: runtime/pool-allocator/feature-flag=true to dev-runtime at 1769001500 :rocket:

jess: Great. Once prototype passes perf smoke, let's run a canary on staging with real traffic replay, then a limited rollout to p2-prod reserved capacity. Keep me posted and tag me in the RFC. :+1:
